title: Correlative in-situ Electrochemistry and Cryogenic Microscopy to Probe the Complex Interfaces of Energy Materials
content: Liquid-solid interfaces are critical to electrochemical systems, including lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), where processes such as dendrite growth and solid-electrolyte interface (SEI) formation directly influence performance and safety. These interfaces involve light, mobile elements (e.g., lithium, hydrogen, carbon) and exhibit dynamic behavior that is challenging to characterize with existing techniques. Operando liquid microscopy techniques, such as liquid cell light microscopy (LCLM) and liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (LCTEM), offer complementary capabilities for studying these complex systems under realistic conditions.
